item.title: Taking Action Against Caravan Organizers Facilitating Illegal Immigration to the United States
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Taking Action Against Caravan Organizers Facilitating Illegal Immigration to the United States

Press Statement

October 29, 2026

The Trump Administration will not tolerate actions that undermine the national security or immigration laws of the United States and is resolute in protecting the integrity of U.S. borders, disrupting smuggling networks, and promoting accountability for those who seek to profit from illegal immigration. That is why the Department of State previously announced a policy to restrict visas to foreign government officials and others who are believed to be responsible for knowingly facilitating illegal immigration to our nation. The Department stands ready to use this policy to take action against individuals who knowingly organize, promote, support, or finance caravans that facilitate illegal immigration to the United States. Any of these individuals or any caravan participants who apply for a U.S. visa or attempt to travel to our nation will face additional scrutiny, and the Department will take appropriate action, which may include refusing or revoking their visas.

Investigations indicate individuals have recruited, coordinated, and directed large groups of immigrants traveling through Central America and Mexico toward the U.S. southern border. In the past week, the Department took steps to impose visa restrictions on more than 15 individuals involved in organizing, facilitating, or promoting recent migrant caravans.

Crossing the U.S. southern border without authorization violates the law and can lead to arrest, detention, deportation, and a future ban on entry to the United States. Those individuals involved in facilitating or participating in such illegal activity will be considered for visa restrictions.

item.title: Secretary Rubio and Hungarian FM Orbán at a MOU Signing Ceremony on Energy Infrastructure and Regional Energy Security and on Law Enforcement Cooperation and Information Exchange
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State, Anita Orbán, Hungarian Foreign Minister
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Anita Orbán, Hungarian Foreign Minister

Washington, DC

Colin L. Powell Treaty Room

Secretary Rubio and Hungarian FM Orbán at a MOU Signing Ceremony on Energy Infrastructure and Regional Energy Security and on Law Enforcement Cooperation and Information Exchange

Remarks

October 29, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, thank you all for covering this here today and for being a part of this.  It’s an honor to be here with Foreign Minister Orbán, and the opportunity to sign these two important agreements.  The first one, of course, is that we are aligned and taking steps together in our governments to confront this resurgence of far-left terrorism, which is something that’s been ignored for far too long.  It’s something I spoke about earlier this year.  And we have to stop the way these groups target police departments and law enforcement, and ultimately critical infrastructure, historical landmarks – the foundations of a free society; that’s what they attack. 

And so this politically – currently this politically motivated violence and destruction of property that we’ve seen in Europe and we’ve seen here in the United States, going back to 2020, where we saw people going after our monuments and going after things important to our history. 

So this will improve – this Memorandum of Understanding, what it does is it’s going to increase cooperation and information sharing.  Because what we have found, as you’ve learned and we’ve learned, is that many of these movements are internationalized.  They operate off the basis of an international network that seeks to destabilize Western societies, our systems, our culture, our civilization, ultimately.  So we’ll work to track these cross-border networks and bring them to justice, and we want to thank Hungary for being such an important partner in Europe in this emerging threat.

The second framework we’re going to sign today has to do on the Trump Peace Pipelines.  It’s another milestone since Secretary Wright announced this at the Three Seas Initiative Summit.  And this is an energy infrastructure initiative that helps to meet Central Europe’s energy needs through U.S. energy.  So this is an opportunity for us to continue to export energy that we are able to develop and create a little bit more energy independence, or at least energy diversification.  So this is important. 

And this memorandum of understanding, in my view, is a testament to the growing strength of the U.S.-Hungary economic cooperation.  It demonstrates how our two countries can work together to deliver tangible results for our citizens. 

So we’re very happy you’re here.  Thank you for joining us and being a part of it.  And I turn it over to you.

FOREIGN MINISTER ORBÁN:  Thank you, Mr. Secretary.  This is such an honor and pleasure to be here at the U.S. State Department, and to work together on enhancing the Hungary and U.S. relationship even further.  And I believe that we can deepen our ties not only in political matters, but security, nuclear, security in general, defense, and economic cooperation. 

And as you said it, we are signing two MOUs today.  The first one we will sign on – which reflects our cooperation against terrorism, against any act of terrorism.  And we will be signing this MOU, which is on combating violent left-wing organizations.  And this is important that under the existing law enforcement cooperation we will enhance the information sharing so that we prevent, detect, and prosecute any violence done by left-wing groups such as Antifa Ost both in the United States and Hungary.

And the second agreement which we will be signing is about energy security and energy infrastructure in Southeast and central Eastern Europe, and the second MOU is – will be within the framework of the U.S. initiative you already mentioned, the Trump Peace Pipelines framework, which is a very important initiative to enhance the energy infrastructure of central Eastern Europe both in oil and gas as well as create options for diversification and alternative sources of supply. 

So we see this cooperation as an important milestone in the Hungary and America energy cooperation, also to help Hungary to become an important player in the regional energy supply, as well as together with you creating a robust, a resilient, and a very competitive energy ecosystem.  The goal of our government is to have predictable, stable, and affordable energy supply for our consumers, for our industry, for our economy, and we see that this cooperation agreement will be a key milestone towards that.

However, I would like to emphasize one more thing: that the MOUs are key milestones, but they are part of the process.  We are driven to take actions, to take action plans, and to have agreements.  And one of the goals of my visit, that I go home today with concrete next steps (inaudible) along both MOUs and more and beyond, because our cooperation goes also beyond.  It encompasses so many fields. 

So I am very much looking forward to our very first official meeting after the signing ceremony, because we have so much to discuss.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.  Okay.  So we’re going to be signing two, right?

STAFF:  Yes.

(The memorandums were signed.)

(Applause.)

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen at a Memorandum of Understanding Signing Ceremony on a Critical Minerals Framework and a Technology Prosperity Deal
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State, Elina Valtonen, Finnish Foreign Minister
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Elina Valtonen, Finnish Foreign Minister

Washington, D.C.

Colin L. Powell Treaty Room

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen at a Memorandum of Understanding Signing Ceremony on a Critical Minerals Framework and a Technology Prosperity Deal

Remarks

October 29, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, welcome.  Thank you.  Thank you for coming here.  Thank you for being here in Washington.  We’re excited to be here today to announce these two agreements and sign these two agreements with Finland, which is a great partner. 

The first one we’re going to sign is the Critical Minerals Framework, which at this point I think is self-explanatory to many people about how important that is.  It’s the foundation of tech, and we’re partnering on that today, everything from semiconductors to batteries to defense systems to energy infrastructure.  All of this is dependent on that, and Finland, of course, has extraordinary expertise in mining, in refining, and in processing that makes it an ideal and critical partner in the world on this topic. 

And then we’ll sign the Technology Prosperity Deal, which is an important milestone in our partnership on critical and emerging technologies today.  And Finland has world-class capabilities in quantum, in telecom, in nuclear, and in nuclear energy, in space systems, in engineering, in biotech.  I mean, you name it, and Finland has world-class capabilities, so it’s an incredibly important partnership for us.

These are two great and important agreements.  We’re very happy that you’re here.  We’re happy to sign it with you, and we look forward to doing even more just in the months and years to come.  So thank you, and welcome to Washington.

FOREIGN MINISTER VALTONEN:  Thank you so much, Marco.  It’s a great honor to be here in Washington D.C. with my colleague, Secretary of State Marco Rubio.  We had a very fruitful and constructive discussion, and this was already our third bilateral meeting in Washington during Secretary Rubio’s tenure.  We have also met several times on the sidelines of the UN and NATO meetings, most recently in New York a month ago during the Arctic allies meeting.  I am very grateful for this strong relationship and the mutually beneficial cooperation between our countries.

The economic ties between Finland and the United States have strengthened substantially in the past decade, particularly Finnish exports to the U.S. and Finnish companies’ investments in the American economy, creating jobs and prosperity.  Key areas of cooperation, like the Secretary mentioned, besides icebreakers as well, include industrial products, connectivity, artificial intelligence, and several other fields of cutting-edge digital technology.  The two-way trade in goods and services has grown by over 60 percent just in the past few years, and the U.S. direct investment in Finland has more than doubled.  The ever-closer Finnish-U.S. security and defense ties have further reinforced the wider economic relationship.

We look forward to fortifying this momentum, and today, with the signing of our two documents, another important milestone.  The Critical Minerals Framework and the Technology Prosperity Deal will deepen mutually beneficial trade, economic, and technological cooperation between our countries, and strengthen our position in the world.

Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  So first we’ll sign the Critical Minerals Framework.

(The Critical Minerals Framework Memorandum of Understanding was signed.)

FOREIGN MINISTER VALTONEN:  For the world to see.

(The Technology Prosperity Deal Memorandum of Understanding was signed.)

FOREIGN MINISTER VALTONEN:  Another day in the office.  (Laughter.)

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.

item.title: The United States Announces Sanctions in Response to Rwanda’s Destabilizing Activities in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

The United States Announces Sanctions in Response to Rwanda’s Destabilizing Activities in Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

Press Statement

October 28, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning Rwanda’s Ministry of Defense and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a financial institution that serves Rwanda’s security services, for supporting the March 23 Movement (M23) armed group in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Thousands of Rwanda Defense Force troops fight alongside M23 in North and South Kivu provinces and have supplied the group with weapons and training. Rwandan troops have also brought in surface-to-air missiles and jamming equipment that endanger civilian aviation.

On December 4, 2025, President Trump brought the leaders of the DRC and Rwanda together to sign the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity (Washington Accords). Both governments agreed to end the conflict and expand trade and investment across the Great Lakes region of Africa. Rwanda’s Ministry of Defense’s support for M23 violates those obligations and undermines the Washington Accords’ goals of peace and prosperity. Rwanda must stop supporting M23 and any successor armed groups and withdraw its forces from eastern DRC. Moreover, armed groups and their state sponsors must not profit from the DRC’s natural resources. In the gold and coltan mining areas under M23 control, including Rubaya in North Kivu, civilians face forced labor, dangerous working conditions, and illegal taxation. We urge our partners and the private sector to examine their supply chains closely. The United States calls on all actors to respect the DRC’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and will use every available tool to hold accountable those who prolong this conflict.

The Rwandan Ministry of Defense is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of the RDF. Zigama is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the RDF, M23, and AFC. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press releases.

item.title: United States Welcomes Vietnam’s Signing of the Artemis Accords
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States Welcomes Vietnam’s Signing of the Artemis Accords

Media Note

October 28, 2026

The U.S. Department of State congratulates the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on joining the Artemis Accords.  Space exploration is entering a new era of discovery and opportunity, with growing importance for scientific advancement, economic growth, and the technologies that will shape the future.  As the 78th signatory, Vietnam joins a growing coalition of nations dedicated to space policy that will extend the reach of human discovery and innovation using safe, transparent, and responsible space exploration and use.  Vietnam will help put these shared principles into practice as a committed partner in the peaceful, cooperative use of space.   

Vietnam’s decision extends the U.S.-Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership into a new frontier.  Built on more than 30 years of cooperation, our partnership spans defense, economic, law enforcement, war legacy, and technological cooperation, and it advances peace, stability, and prosperity in a free and open Indo-Pacific.

Vietnam’s Minister of Science and Technology Vũ Hải Quân signed the Accords on behalf of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on October 28, 2026.  U.S. Ambassador to Vietnam Jennifer Wicks witnessed and celebrated the signing at a ceremony on the margins of Vietnam International Digital Week in Ha Long, Vietnam.

The United States and seven other countries established the Artemis Accords in 2020 during President Trump’s first term to serve as a set of practical principles to guide responsible space exploration.  The U.S. Department of State and NASA lead the United States’ outreach and implementation of the Accords.

For more information, including a full list of signatories to the Accords, please visit the Artemis Accords webpage.  For media inquiries, please submit a request.

item.title: Czech Republic National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Czech Republic National Day

Press Statement

October 28, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the Czech people as you celebrate the anniversary of your independence in 1918.

Our two nations share a commitment to building prosperity, free speech, liberty, and national sovereignty. The Czech Republic is a capable and trusted security partner. Both of our nations understand and are committed to a strong NATO, which will require increased investment over the coming decade for each ally to meet the Hague commitment. We also value our close cooperation on energy security, which strengthens the dynamism and resilience of our nations.

American and Czech companies continue to deepen our commercial ties as they invest in each other’s markets and create jobs for our workers. Together, we will build on this momentum to make the future more prosperous for Americans and Czechs alike. I wish all Czechs a memorable celebration.

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau hosted Tonga Prime Minister Lord Fakafanua for a meeting today in Washington, DC continuing their productive conversations from the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders’ Meeting in September. The Deputy Secretary and the Prime Minister reaffirmed the strong and longstanding bonds of friendship between the two countries and discussed ongoing cooperation to strengthen economic and commercial ties, including digital and energy infrastructure.

Office of the Spokesman

Secretary Rubio’s Call with Panama President Mulino

Readout

October 27, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino to discuss earthquake recovery, regional issues, and the UN Secretary General election. The call reaffirmed the deepening U.S.-Panama partnership following the October 9 earthquake. Secretary Rubio emphasized that the American people will continue to stand firmly with Panama through its recovery. He noted our strong relationship allowed the United States to deliver humanitarian, logistics, communication, and technical assistance – including food, water, and urban search and rescue teams – to affected communities within 24 hours.
